As the news of the disaster spread, authorities scrambled to respond to the crisis, but their efforts were in vain. The city's infrastructure, including roads, buildings, and utilities, was left in ruins, and the population seemed to have vanished into thin air.

"It's as if the city never existed," said Dr. John Smith, a local geologist who was studying the area when the disaster occurred. "The landscape has returned to its pre-industrial state, with forests and wildlife reclaiming the area. It's a truly surreal sight."

Families who were in the city at the time of the disaster are still trying to come to terms with what happened, but many seem to have forgotten the entire event.

"I was at home with my family when the explosion happened," said John Johnson, a local resident who was in the area when the disaster occurred. "We were all shaken, but then... nothing. We just went about our daily lives as if nothing had happened. It's like we're living in a dream."
